title: Use AKS-managed Microsoft Entra ID authentication
description: Authenticate users to the Kubernetes API with AKS-managed Microsoft Entra ID integration and group-based access. Migrate legacy integration and validate administrator group access before disabling local accounts. Authentication establishes identity; configure Kubernetes or Azure RBAC separately for authorization.

documentation.title: Microsoft Entra ID control plane authentication

title: Choose and scope Kubernetes RBAC or Azure RBAC for Kubernetes authorization
description: Use Microsoft Entra groups with Kubernetes Roles/RoleBindings, or Azure RBAC for Kubernetes Authorization, to grant least-privilege access at namespace scope where possible. Distinguish Kubernetes data-plane permissions from Azure management-plane roles that retrieve kubeconfig or change the cluster. Review cluster-admin bindings and privilege-escalation paths regularly.

documentation.title: Microsoft Entra ID with Kubernetes RBAC

title: Use AKS and ACR integration without password
description: Use the kubelet managed identity to pull images from Azure Container Registry instead of registry admin credentials or long-lived image pull secrets. Grant only the required registry or repository access.
detail: For RBAC-only registries, AKS ACR integration assigns AcrPull to the kubelet identity. For registries using RBAC Registry + ABAC Repository Permissions, --attach-acr is not supported: assign Container Registry Repository Reader manually, with repository conditions where appropriate. Workload identity for application Azure API calls is separate from kubelet image-pull authentication.

documentation.title: Authenticate with Azure Container Registry from AKS

title: Use least-privilege managed identities for cluster and kubelet access
detail: Review effective Azure role assignments, scopes and inherited grants for the actual control-plane and kubelet identities, including network and registry access. Confirm representative operations succeed and unauthorized operations are denied; a managed-identity flag alone does not demonstrate least privilege.
description: Prefer system-assigned or user-assigned managed identities over cluster service principals to avoid credential rotation. Separate control-plane resource management permissions from kubelet image-pull permissions, scope grants to required resources and do not reuse node identities for application access. During identity migration, retain necessary old grants until token refresh and validation complete.

documentation.title: Use managed identities in Azure Kubernetes Service

title: Limit access to admin kubeconfig (get-credentials --admin)
description: Restrict Azure permissions to retrieve cluster-admin credentials, update identity settings, invoke AKS Run Command or manage nodes. Prefer user kubeconfig with Microsoft Entra authentication; retrieving user kubeconfig does not itself grant Kubernetes authorization. Audit privileged management operations and keep an approved, tested emergency access procedure.

documentation.title: Use Azure RBAC to define access to the Kubernetes configuration file

title: For AKS non-interactive logins use kubelogin
description: Use kubelogin's supported exec authentication modes for automation. Prefer managed identity on Azure-hosted agents or federated workload identity for CI over service principal secrets. Grant the automation identity only required cluster permissions and ensure it has network access to the API server; avoid interactive/device-code flows in pipelines.

title: Disable AKS local accounts
description: Disable local accounts after validating Microsoft Entra administrator and automation access so static administrator credentials cannot bypass identity controls. On existing clusters, rotate cluster certificates to revoke previously issued local credentials. Document tightly controlled emergency re-enablement, audit its use and disable local accounts again after recovery.

title: Use Privileged Identity Management for just-in-time privileged access
description: Use Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management for eligible, time-limited administrative role or group activation with approval and MFA as appropriate. Scope access separately for Kubernetes administration and node access, review activations and account for Microsoft Entra licensing requirements.

documentation.title: Control AKS cluster and node access with PIM

title: Precreate a user-assigned kubelet identity when permissions are needed before provisioning
description: Use a precreated user-assigned kubelet identity when registry permissions or group membership must exist before cluster creation. Grant the control-plane identity the required permission to assign it, especially outside the node resource group, and allow role propagation time. A kubelet identity is not a pod workload identity.

documentation.title: AKS managed identity types and authorization

title: Apply Microsoft Entra Conditional Access to human cluster sign-ins
description: Apply appropriate MFA, device and location requirements to Microsoft Entra-authenticated administrator sign-ins. Validate kubelogin authentication flows and emergency access before enforcement, and review licensing. Do not assume user Conditional Access policies protect local certificate credentials or workload identities.

title: Use Microsoft Entra Workload ID and migrate retired pod-managed identity
applicability: Applies to pods requiring supported Azure service authentication, including deployments migrating from retired pod-managed identity.
description: Use Microsoft Entra Workload ID for pod-to-Azure authentication without stored credentials. Azure AD Pod Identity was deprecated on October 24, 2022 and its project archived in September 2023; support for the AKS managed add-on ran through September 2025. Migrate remaining bindings and applications instead of deploying it.
detail: Enable the OIDC issuer and workload identity on AKS Standard (preconfigured on AKS Automatic). Configure dedicated Kubernetes service accounts, exact federated issuer/namespace/service-account subject/audience bindings, the azure.workload.identity/use: true pod label and supported Azure Identity SDK or MSAL versions. Grant only required Azure data-plane permissions per workload, test token renewal and remove old pod identity components and node identity grants only after successful migration.
